text: Efferent [Lat. ex + ferre , to bear]: Ger. centrifugal ; Fr. efférent ; Ital. efferente . The term applied to those nerves (also termed centrifugal) which carry impulses outward from the central nervous system; also to the impulses so transmitted. Suggested by W. B. Carpenter (1842), Human Physiol . (1st ed.), 83. It is opposed to AFFERENT, or CENTRIPETAL (see those terms). ( C.LL.M. )
